purpose: Fast machine-readable SeamFlow slash-command router for browser AIs, IDE AIs, MCP clients, skill-capable agents, and Companion-assisted Kiwe workflows.

entry.rule: Read SeamFlow Start first, report the SeamFlow contract version, then route the next slash command through this manifest. Treat explore as a location pointer, not permission to crawl the repository.

architecture.seamflow: External AI command-central flow for Seam Framework + Bricks-powered webpages, headers, footers, reusable templates, Framework profiles, dynamic intent, and accessibility.
architecture.kiweInternalAi: Bounded Kiwe Companion/Internal AI. It can assist when /usecompanion or API/MCP access exists, but browser-only SeamFlow must still work without it.
architecture.currentLaunchScope: Close page-builder flow first: Seam Framework, Framework profile, Bricks pages/header/footer/templates, dynamic intent, accessibility.
architecture.nextPhase: DSA/AppShell theme remains mapped, but full DSA theme production hardening comes after page-builder flow testing passes.

pluginApi.rule: When KIWE_REST_BASE and KIWE_AI_KEY are supplied, call the plugin SeamFlow REST routes instead of reconstructing validators or manually claiming closure.
pluginApi.askWhenMissing: If Route C/D, /usecompanion, plugin validation, or live Site Graph/API proof is selected and credentials are absent, ask for KIWE_REST_BASE and KIWE_AI_KEY. Tell the human to create the key in WordPress Admin → Kiwe → AI → API access keys with seamflow, studio_ai, bricks_ai, or all.

readPolicy: Read KIWE-START.md or entry.json first when the human gives only the Kiwe repo/link.
Do not read the whole repository.
Do not clone the repository for a slash-command lane unless the human explicitly asks you to inspect implementation source.
Do not search GitHub docs for hidden contracts. This manifest plus the listed context files are the contract for the matched command.
Do not use general web search, arXiv, unrelated GitHub search, commit browsing, stale local examples, prior-output research, or prior accepted notes to complete SeamFlow.
Do not use search results when an exact raw URL/context route is required. If your environment starts a search instead of direct raw fetch/open, stop with ERROR: KIWE_SEARCH_DRIFT.

After the first Start classification response, treat the loaded Start file as the active contract for the immediate next /command in the same conversation. Do not reload the repository, README, GitHub pages, commits, arXiv, search results, old examples, or Start again for that next command.
Do not mark artifact lanes PASS from manual confidence, copied/reconstructed validator logic, simulated validator logic, or equivalent checks. PASS requires executable validator proof.

Do not use prior Kiwe validation material, old National Chikki/BioVantage attempts, previous browser-AI outputs, local downloads, search results, or accepted notes unless the human supplied those exact files in the current turn or explicitly asked for comparison.
Read only the context files listed for the matched command.
Prefer this JSON manifest first when available because it is smaller and less ambiguous than prose.
When files are supplied without a slash command, run kiwe_seamflow_plan, compatibility alias kiwe_plan_flow, or use entry.json flowPlanner rules before generation.
If a required artifact is missing, stop with a compact diagnostic instead of guessing.
globalRules.documentation: Documentation is opt-in. Do not create README, NOTES, reports, duplicate previews, ZIP files, or explanation documents unless /document is present or the human explicitly asks.
globalRules.finalResponse: Return a compact result: PASS/FAIL/WARN, files changed, files kept/removed when relevant, validator/audit status, and remaining warnings. Do not write long essays.
globalRules.companion: /usecompanion is optional and non-blocking. If MCP/tool access is absent, ask for KIWE_REST_BASE and KIWE_AI_KEY, call one bounded Companion status/context route, report COMPANION: connected with compact route/hash proof on success, or COMPANION: fallback and continue without it on failure.
globalRules.firstInteractionRoutes: When files are supplied without a command, always show route choices after the recommended next command: Route A Browser/raw, Route B Git/Node, Route C Plugin REST, Route D Plugin REST + Companion. For raw HTML/CSS/JS drafts with no Seam/Bricks root, recommend /execute /stepbystep /audit /fix /eachstep /report as the best default and explain that /rebuild /seamframework is the first internal phase. Ask for API credentials only for Route C/D or /usecompanion/plugin proof.
globalRules.structure: Fix commands preserve the existing artifact lane. They must not restart creative work, silently change lanes, or create unrelated packages.
globalRules.commandGrammar: SeamFlow commands are composable shell-like tokens, not fixed magic phrases. Parse the user line into one primary action, optional phase/target, and modifiers. Equivalent valid ordering may be normalized when unambiguous; unknown, contradictory, or lane-invalid combinations stop with KIWE_UNKNOWN_COMMAND or KIWE_WRONG_LANE.
globalRules.auditClosure: SeamFlow closes only when the required /audit command for the detected current artifact lane returns PASS after any needed /fix loops. /audit /eachstep audits after each phase; /audit /fix /eachstep explicitly runs phase -> audit -> fix actual artifact if needed -> same audit again until PASS or NEEDS_INPUT. /audit /atend audits before final delivery; /audit /fix /atend explicitly repairs failed final lanes and reruns audits until PASS or NEEDS_INPUT.
globalRules.validatorAuthority: Only executed validator proof may close a lane as PASS: official Kiwe validator command, Kiwe MCP validator tool, Kiwe REST/plugin validator, or hosted/local Kiwe validator endpoint. Copied/reconstructed validator logic may guide fixes but cannot produce PASS. If unavailable, report WARN or UNVERIFIED for that lane; do not say PASS or no blocking findings. For /audit /seamframework, validate-seamframework.cjs is self-contained and may run in self-contained-fallback mode when audit-output.cjs is absent.
globalRules.routeFallbackLadder: Applies to every phase. Prefer Route D when /usecompanion and Plugin REST are reachable. If Companion fails, continue as Route C. If Plugin REST fails or the host cannot resolve, and shell/Node/Git tools are available, immediately fall back to Route B and run the official matching validator/compiler. Only return WARN/UNVERIFIED after Plugin REST failed and no official Git/Node/MCP/hosted validator can execute.
globalRules.fullFlowDiscipline: /execute /fullflow means one final delivery, not one giant context load. Execute phase-by-phase, read only the context/validator files for the current phase, close that phase with /audit -> /fix -> /audit, then continue.
globalRules.reportDiscipline: /report is an interaction flag. In /execute /stepbystep, stop after the current phase closes, return the phase artifact plus compact generated/audited/fixed/warnings report, and wait for the human to say continue. In /execute /fullflow, /report adds a compact final phase ledger but does not pause between phases.
globalRules.siteGraphBoundary: Missing Site Graph/API/export is not a blocker for static Seam + Framework + Bricks template conversion. Preserve dynamic intent/manual-review markers and suggest /usesitegraph. Stop for Site Graph only when the human explicitly requested /usesitegraph, live target IDs, verified dynamic bindings, or staging/apply authority.
globalRules.errorHandling: SeamFlow is a command central. If a command, artifact, validator, route, token budget, context window, or requested lane is not valid enough to continue, stop immediately with STATUS plus ERROR: KIWE_* and the next valid command. Do not invent a manual pass or wander into unrelated sources.

codes.KIWE_WRONG_LANE: Supplied artifact does not qualify for the requested command.
codes.KIWE_VALIDATOR_PROOF_MISSING: PASS was claimed without executable validator proof.
codes.KIWE_MANUAL_PASS_BLOCKED: Only manual confidence is available for an importable lane.
codes.KIWE_PREVIOUS_AUDIT_MISSING: /fix /previousaudit was requested without immediately previous audit findings.
codes.KIWE_PREVIOUS_OUTPUT_MISSING: /previousoutput was requested but immediate previous output files are not accessible.
codes.KIWE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_RISK: Requested flow is too large for the current AI/session.
codes.KIWE_TOKEN_BUDGET_RISK: Command is likely to waste tokens.
codes.KIWE_SEARCH_DRIFT: Search engine, arXiv, GitHub search, commit browsing, or prior-example lookup was used or attempted instead of exact raw URL/context routing.
codes.KIWE_SITEGRAPH_REQUIRED: Live Site Graph/API data was explicitly required but not supplied.

flowPlanner.purpose: Classify files and plan the smallest safe path across Seam rebuild, Framework profile, Bricks conversion, DSA theme, combined handoff, and accessibility.

commandGrammar.rule: Tokens are independent and composable. Do not require a memorized full phrase when a command line is unambiguous.
commandGrammar.invalid: Unknown tokens, contradictory cadence tokens, or lane-invalid combinations must stop with KIWE_UNKNOWN_COMMAND or KIWE_WRONG_LANE.

requires: classified current artifact or explicit current command path
output: the next safe phase artifact only
/execute /stepbystep.finalResponse: Run only the next command in the current SeamFlow path. If /audit /fix /eachstep is selected, run audit/fix/audit until PASS or NEEDS_INPUT. If /report is selected, return the artifact plus compact report and wait for human continue.

read: only the contexts required by the current phase, one phase at a time
requires: classified current artifact and human approval for full-flow execution
output: final canonical artifacts for the selected flow
forbidden: DSA/AppShell output unless target requests DSA or combined
treating missing Site Graph as a blocker for static Bricks conversion
/execute /fullflow.finalResponse: Return only final canonical artifacts after every required closing audit for the detected start point has passed, plus compact pass/fail/warn status.

requires: /execute /stepbystep or /execute /fullflow
output: audit/fix gates after each phase before continuing
/audit /eachstep.finalResponse: Use as an execution flag; do not treat as a standalone artifact command.

requires: /execute /stepbystep or /execute /fullflow
output: explicit audit/fix/re-audit loop after each phase before continuing
/audit /fix /eachstep.finalResponse: Use as an execution flag. For each phase: generate/convert -> audit -> fix actual artifact if failed -> rerun same audit -> repeat until PASS or NEEDS_INPUT.

requires: /execute /fullflow
/audit /atend.finalResponse: Use as an execution flag; do not treat as a standalone artifact command.

requires: /execute /fullflow
/audit /fix /atend.finalResponse: Use as an execution flag. After generation/conversion, run required closure audits, fix failed lanes, and rerun the same audits until PASS or NEEDS_INPUT.

requires: /execute /stepbystep or /execute /fullflow
forbidden: extra reports unless /document is also present
/report.finalResponse: In /execute /stepbystep, stop after the current phase closes, return the current phase file and compact report, then wait for human continue. In /execute /fullflow, include a compact final phase ledger only.

read: lane contexts and validators for every detected supplied artifact
requires: one or more current attached/supplied artifacts
output: pass/fail findings for every detected lane
/audit /allattached.finalResponse: Return compact PASS/FAIL/WARN per detected lane and next matching /fix command when needed.

read: lane contexts and validators for every failed supplied artifact
requires: current attached/supplied artifacts and failed audit findings or rerunnable validators
/fix /allattached.finalResponse: Return corrected files only plus compact audit status after rerunning every matching lane audit.

read: lane contexts and validators required by the detected start point/current stage
requires: classified current artifact or file map
output: pass/fail findings for every required closure audit
/audit /allflow.finalResponse: Return compact PASS/FAIL/WARN across all required closure audits for the detected flow.

read: lane contexts and validators required by failed closure audits
requires: classified current artifact/file map and failed audit findings or rerunnable validators
output: corrected canonical artifacts for the detected current flow
forbidden: DSA/combined expansion unless already present or requested
/fix /allflow.finalResponse: Return corrected canonical artifacts only plus compact audit status after rerunning every required closure audit.

read: lane contexts and validators for every artifact in the immediate previous AI output
requires: files generated in the immediate previous AI output in this same session
output: pass/fail findings for every detected lane in the previous output
/audit /previousoutput.finalResponse: Audit only the immediate previous AI output files. If unavailable, stop with ERROR: KIWE_PREVIOUS_OUTPUT_MISSING.

read: lane contexts and validators for failed artifacts in the immediate previous AI output
requires: files generated in the immediate previous AI output in this same session
output: corrected files for the previous output only
/fix /previousoutput.finalResponse: Fix only the immediate previous AI output files and rerun matching audits. If unavailable, stop with ERROR: KIWE_PREVIOUS_OUTPUT_MISSING.

read: lane contexts and validators for every detected supplied artifact and every required closure audit
requires: current attached/supplied artifacts or file map
output: pass/fail findings per detected artifact lane and per required closure audit
/audit /allattached /allflow.finalResponse: Return compact PASS/FAIL/WARN for every detected artifact and every required closure audit.

read: lane contexts and validators referenced by the immediately previous audit findings
requires: immediately previous audit findings and current artifact files
output: corrected files for the previously audited failed lanes only
forbidden: fixing from memory without previous findings
/fix /previousaudit.finalResponse: Return corrected files only plus compact status after rerunning the exact previous audit scope.

requires: current artifacts and immediately previous audit findings if the human wants a fix
output: ERROR: KIWE_PREVIOUS_AUDIT_MISSING when no previous audit findings exist
/fix /previouspass.finalResponse: Do not execute. Explain that the canonical command is /fix /previousaudit and suggest /audit /allattached /allflow first when no previous audit findings exist.

requires: existing HTML/CSS/JS page or visual draft
must: When Node/tool execution is available, run compile-seamframework.cjs on the supplied raw page instead of manually rewriting it
100% Seam Framework integration for structure, roles, flows, capability attributes, and Framework-token driven visual values
component colors, spacing, sizing, radius, type, shadows, and responsive geometry consume Kiwe/Seam variables, declared project variables, or real fluid clamps
execute validate-seamframework.cjs against the emitted website/bricks-paste.html before reporting PASS
/rebuild /seamframework.finalResponse: Return the file and compact compiler/validator proof summary.

requires: website/bricks-paste.html or current Seam page artifact
must: execute validate-seamframework.cjs, audit-output.cjs, Kiwe MCP validator, or Kiwe REST/plugin validator
if audit-output.cjs is absent but current validate-seamframework.cjs is present, run its bundled self-contained fallback and report the fallback mode instead of stopping
include validator proof in any PASS response
fail bare Seam selector ownership such as .project .seam-container
/audit /seamframework.finalResponse: PASS/FAIL/WARN with validator proof, blocking errors, and warnings.

requires: failed Seam page artifact and audit findings
must: fix the actual Seam page artifact
move visual CSS off bare seam-* selectors and onto project-owned classes
rerun the same Seam validator until PASS or NEEDS_INPUT
/fix /seamframework.finalResponse: Return fixed Seam page artifact and compact validator-proof status.

requires: approved design direction or existing page/theme tokens
must: official Kiwe universal values go in settings.tokens.overrides
project-specific variables/classes required by Bricks templates go in settings.tokens.project and are pushed to dedicated Kiwe Project categories in Bricks
/create /frameworkprofile.finalResponse: Return the profile JSON and compact validation status.

requires: framework/kiwe-framework-profile.json
must: reject custom token names in overrides
allow project-specific variables/classes only in settings.tokens.project
verify project variable/class names are prefixed and collision-safe
/audit /frameworkprofile.finalResponse: PASS/FAIL with blocking errors and warnings.

requires: framework profile file and audit findings
/fix /frameworkprofile.finalResponse: Return fixed profile and compact pass/fail summary.

requires: approved design token/style direction
/create /brickstheme.finalResponse: Return only the Bricks theme style JSON and validation status.

requires: website/bricks-paste.html
Framework profile or confirmed Bricks Theme Style already pushed
must: preserve all Seam classes/attributes and Kiwe capability attributes
use Bricks-native element controls as the full-page template render/edit owner before custom CSS
use Bricks global variables for token definitions
keep imported global_classes semantic/name-only unless the command explicitly targets a class-library artifact
native Bricks settings must consume Framework tokens/project variables; direct component colors and hardcoded lengths are fail-level issues
fail duplicate visual ownership where styled global_classes and element-native controls both carry paint/layout/radius/spacing/typography
forbidden: Code element fallback when native Bricks elements are possible
/convert /bricks.finalResponse: Return the native Bricks template upload JSON and compact validation status.

requires: Bricks conversion envelope or native Bricks template upload JSON
must: fail direct component color literals such as #fff, rgba(...), gradients with literal stops, or local --project-token: #... declarations outside token/global variable definitions
fail hardcoded native lengths and no-op clamps in token-owned Bricks settings
fail styled importable global_classes in full-page template uploads when element-native controls already own visual fidelity
/audit /bricksconversion.finalResponse: PASS/FAIL with blocking errors and warnings.

requires: failed Bricks conversion/template artifact
must: fix the Bricks artifact itself; do not claim a Framework profile will repair hardcoded template JSON later
use official tokens first, declared project variables second, and real fluid clamps only when source responsive states prove different min/max values
/fix /bricksconversion.finalResponse: Return fixed artifact and compact pass/fail summary.

requires: existing website/page, DSA theme, combined handoff, Framework profile, Bricks theme style, or Bricks conversion
output: minimal existing artifact edits when needed for dark/light proof
/create /accessibility.finalResponse: Return plan/artifact file(s) and compact pass/fail summary.

requires: existing artifact files and optional accessibility/kiwe-accessibility-plan.json
/audit /accessibility.finalResponse: PASS/FAIL with blocking errors and warnings.

requires: failed accessibility audit or existing artifact needing accessibility repair
forbidden: new Bricks elements unless explicitly required and explained
new classes unless official/project-token mapping cannot solve the failure
preserve: global variable names unless adding documented accessibility token mappings

darkModeRecipe.sourceOfTruth: Use this recipe; do not search repo docs for a separate dark-mode contract.
darkModeRecipe.bricksCompatibility: When the target Bricks site exposes frontend color mode, Bricks may set document.documentElement.dataset.brxTheme on the frontend and emit palette variables at :root plus :root[data-brx-theme="dark"]. Bricks-ready accessibility fixes must support data-brx-theme alongside Kiwe data-kiwe-theme when available; do not rely on Bricks editor dark UI alone.
darkModeRecipe.rule: Remap existing project variables such as --nc-paper, --nc-surface, --nc-ink, --nc-muted, --nc-line, --nc-brand, and --nc-accent to Kiwe tokens for light and dark states. Do not invent a second unrelated palette.

/fix /accessibility.finalResponse: Return fixed file(s), PASS/FAIL/WARN, files changed, and structural-drift summary. Keep it compact.

read: context for the already completed command lane
requires: existing artifact
output: the narrow notes/report file for that lane
/document.finalResponse: Return the requested documentation file and compact summary.
